Foo Fighters Debut New Song “Window” on Jimmy Kimmel Live and Reflect on Taylor Hawkins’ Legacy

Performance Overview

On Monday night, Foo Fighters took the stage of *Jimmy Kimmel Live!* for the first of a four‑night residency, delivering a stripped‑down rendition of the brand‑new track “Window.” The quintet opened with a relaxed, almost southern‑rock groove that lingered for a few verses before the arrangement fell into a dramatic pause. In the silence, frontman Dave Grohl sang the lyric, “I saw your face, there in the window / You were a window cleaner,” before concluding the brief song with a modest guitar solo. The performance was notable not only for the song’s debut but also for the band’s decision to play a different track each night of the week‑long stint, a format that gives fans a fresh listening experience and showcases the group’s diverse catalog.

Song “Window”: Inspiration and Composition

During an extended interview with Kimmel, Grohl explained the personal origins of “Window.” He said the song began as a simple idea he could share with his 17‑year‑old daughter, Harper, who was just learning bass. “I thought, ‘I’m gonna write a song … that she can come upstairs and put a bass line on, like really simple, and then we can jam together,’” Grohl told the host. He added that Harper’s favorite band, the Breeders, influenced the track’s vibe, prompting him to aim for a sound that felt “kind of like the Breeders.”

The lyrical concept emerged from a vivid, everyday scene: a hotel room, curtains drawn back, and a window cleaner entering the space. Grohl described the moment as a glimpse into people’s most private moments, noting, “I realized that window cleaners witness people’s most intimate moments and wrote a song about it.” The result is a concise, narrative‑driven rock song that balances a light‑hearted melody with an oddly voyeuristic lyric.

A Tribute to Taylor Hawkins

The interview also turned reflective as Grolin discussed his long‑standing friendship with the late drummer Taylor Hawkins. Grohl recounted their first meeting at a 1995 KROQ‑hosted event called *Almost Acoustic Christmas*, where Hawkins was then playing drums for Alanis Morissette. “Our first record came out around the time Alanis’ first record came out,” Grohl said, recalling the overlapping timelines of the two artists. He described Hawkins as a “blond, surfer dude” who approached him backstage with enthusiastic praise for the band. That encounter, Grohl explained, sparked an instant connection: “I knew, right then, I was like, ‘Oh, we’re gonna be best friends for the rest of our lives.’”

The two musicians crossed paths again at subsequent gigs where Foo Fighters opened for Morissette, and Hawkins later shared a backstage anecdote about a flight from France. According to Grohl, Morissette asked Hawkins what he would do if Grohl ever asked him to join Foo Fighters as a drummer. Hawkins replied, “What are you going to do when Dave asks you to be the drummer?” Grohl recalled telling Morissette, “No, baby, I love you,” before Hawkins officially became the band’s drummer within six months. While the conversation was light‑hearted, it underscored the deep personal bond that would define the band’s rhythm section for decades until Hawkins’ untimely death in 2022.

The Kimmel Residency and Fan Reception

Foo Fighters’ decision to perform a different song each night on *Jimmy Kimmel Live!* is a rare promotional strategy for a major rock act. By offering a rotating setlist, the band creates a sense of event television that encourages repeat viewership and social‑media discussion. Early fan reactions on platforms such as Twitter and Reddit highlighted excitement over hearing “Window” for the first time, as well as appreciation for the band’s willingness to spotlight lesser‑known tracks alongside classic hits.

The residency also serves a practical purpose: it gives the group a chance to test new material in a live‑television environment before a broader tour rollout. For fans, the format provides a glimpse of what a future setlist might look like and offers a shared experience that can be streamed or re‑watched. As of the article’s publication, the band has not announced whether any of the other three songs performed later in the week will be released as singles or added to an upcoming album.

What’s Next and How to Verify

While the Rolling Stone piece confirms the performance details, the interview’s broader implications remain open‑ended. Listeners can verify the exact lyrics and arrangement of “Window” by watching the *Jimmy Kimmel Live!* broadcast on the show’s official YouTube channel or on the network’s streaming platform. The full interview with Dave Grohl is also available on the same outlet, providing context for his comments about Harper, the Breeders, and the window‑cleaner narrative.

For those interested in the band’s ongoing tribute to Taylor Hawkins, Foo Fighters have previously released a live album titled *Live at Wembley Stadium* (2022) that includes a heartfelt performance of “Everlong” dedicated to Hawkins. The band’s official website and social‑media accounts frequently post archival footage and statements that further illuminate Hawkins’ influence on their sound and camaraderie.

In summary, Foo Fighters’ debut of “Window” on *Jimmy Kimmel Live!* blends fresh songwriting with personal storytelling, while the interview segment offers a poignant look back at the friendship that shaped the band’s rhythm section. The four‑night residency not only showcases the group’s musical versatility but also invites fans to engage directly with new material in real time. As the week progresses, viewers can continue to track the band’s setlist evolution and anticipate how “Window” might fit into future releases or live shows.
